scope: Adaptive learning in macroeconomics: the Robbins-Siegmund lemma; almost sure convergence of stochastic approximation with a quadratic Lyapunov function; the cobweb model under steady-state (least-squares) learning, learnable iff beta < 1 (E-stability), E-unstable divergence for beta > 1, naive expectations exploding for |beta| > 1, the cobweb market from demand and supply primitives; E-stability of linear models in Lyapunov form, its sufficient conditions, the eigenvalue obstruction, uniqueness and existence of the REE, and almost sure convergence of steady-state learning to E-stable REE.
source: Robbins and Monro (1951); Robbins and Siegmund (1971); Muth (1961); Bray and Savin (1986); Marcet and Sargent (1989); Evans and Honkapohja, Learning and Expectations in Macroeconomics (2001).
